gate_results.gate: Authority conflicts: canon, timeline, state, viewpoint knowledge
gate_results.evidence: The rewrite invents a restriction that conflicts with the immediately preceding rewritten seam: chapter 28 says Taren was “not cleared to set foot in Meridian,” while chapter 27 places him on Meridian’s landing. Professor Kim’s disputed pronouns are prudently avoided and therefore remain a human canon question rather than a new contradiction.

gate_results.gate: Assigned obligations: chapter function, plants, payoffs, prohibited outcomes
gate_results.evidence: Kade publicly chooses to turn away from the exit and says “Eli’s worth it”; NULL-7 delivers “DUDE. / DO NOT FREAK OUT.” The loose name, unresolved device, watched traffic, fellowship custody, and move-to-Mara end state are preserved without revealing Ghost Protocol.

The opening and memorial decision are materially reconceived, but the post-memorial Ortiz/Sera and Kim/Kade sequence remains substantially mapped to the source in order, informational beats, dialogue functions, and several close formulations. The prior HIGH freshness defect is narrowed but not fully repaired.

Kade’s public turn is caused by his established flight reflex, Hale’s offered exit, and Kade’s prior shuttle-gate lesson. His belief in the NULL-7 message proceeds by explicit evidence testing rather than convenient certainty.

gate_results.gate: Progression 1 — intelligible cause and recorded delta
gate_results.evidence: Human progression is explicit: Kade converts his established habit of leaving into a public choice to stay, acknowledge dependence, and seek Mara rather than act alone.
Kade’s admission carries visible grief, failed speech, shaking hands, anger at Sen, and renewed vulnerability.

gate_results.gate: Progression 3 — progress outside the measuring system
gate_results.evidence: The change is relational and behavioral, not numerical: public acknowledgment of Eli, acceptance of Mara’s support, and collaborative response to the message.

gate_results.gate: Progression 4 — no unestablished capability resolves victory
gate_results.evidence: No power resolves the chapter. The turn depends on choice, testimony, prior evidence, and relationship.

gate_results.gate: Progression 5 — rivals and institutions remain active
gate_results.evidence: The Hall, fellowship committee, security supervision, response department, and Sen’s concealment all retain independent rules and motives.
The chapter’s social and moral challenge differs from prior combat/training problems and tests Kade through public grief and trust.

gate_results.gate: Progression 7 — setbacks change behavior or understanding
gate_results.evidence: Eli’s apparent death changes Kade’s behavior: he rejects preemptive detachment, speaks publicly, and chooses evidence-sharing with Mara.
Kade can leave through the opened door or speak; later he can confront Sen, keep the secret alone, or involve Mara.
Leaving protects Kade from public exposure; speaking honors Eli and connection. Secrecy protects Eli from watchers while involving Mara protects evidence quality and Kade from isolation.
The text identifies costs borne by Kade, Eli’s family, Taren, Sera, civilian departments, and the intended users of Eli’s design.
Kade refuses to convert the loose name or missing device into hope, then treats the messages as evidence and tests them within his available knowledge.
Sera, Taren, Mara, Julian, Ortiz, Kim, and Sen pursue distinct purposes and behave through established relationship-specific strategies.
Taren’s strip does not restore trust; Eli’s work retains ownership constraints; Sen’s deception produces simultaneous rage and relief.
Neither Taren’s rescue acts nor Sen’s protective secrecy erase relational harm.

gate_results.gate: Character, emotional movement, and voice charter
gate_results.evidence: Kade moves from task-bound guardedness through an attempted exit to public vulnerability and evidence-disciplined hope. Practical attention, clean humor, and distinct voices fit the selected voice.
Speaker turns, scene transitions, names, and message sequence remain intelligible aloud; no profanity, explicit sexual material, gore, metadata, or new named character appears.
Deterministic count is 5,141 words, within the declared 4,048–5,152 range.

draft_evidence.quote: Captain Ortiz gives Sera the failed housing for diagnosis, discloses six housings/four cables and the responder recovery, reveals Eli’s replacement connector and unaffordable certification rig, then offers supervised unpaid work; Professor Kim immediately follows with the collaborator wafer, cost-assumption warning, family/working-group custody limits, thirty-day hold, and “suspended” fellowship.

comparison_evidence.quote: The source presents the same consecutive courtyard construction: Ortiz gives Sera the housing, walks through the same failure history and certification problem, offers supervised unpaid work subject to family/committee permission, after which Kim gives Kade the proposal wafer, cost-assumption warning, custody limits, thirty-day hold, and suspended fellowship.

findings.consequence: Although the chapter’s opening, Taren staging, testimony order, speech approach, and NULL-7 proof are fresher, this long post-memorial movement still reproduces the source’s scene order and nearly every dramatic beat. A reader comparing editions receives a reconstructed version of the same two conversations rather than genuinely fresh staging, so the verified freshness obligation remains materially unmet.
findings.repair_target: Rebuild the post-memorial delivery of the Ortiz and fellowship obligations. Preserve the Denver failure facts, custody boundaries, Sera opportunity, Kade collaborator duty, and suspended status, but change the dramatic vehicle, participant arrangement, order, and conversational progression rather than retaining two consecutive source-shaped handoffs.

findings.gate: Authority conflicts: canon, timeline, state, viewpoint knowledge

draft_evidence.quote: He was cleared to attend under escort and not cleared to set foot in Meridian, so this was the first place he could have asked.

comparison_evidence.quote: Taren was on the landing, standing well out from the wall with his hands in plain view. “You’ll have seen the sheet,” he said.

findings.consequence: The newly asserted access restriction makes Taren’s presence on Meridian’s landing in the immediately preceding chapter impossible or unexplained, creating a visible seam contradiction introduced solely to support the relocated strip request.
findings.repair_target: Remove the absolute claim that Taren was barred from Meridian, or replace it with a motive consistent with his prior escorted presence, such as choosing not to enter the House or being asked to meet them at the Hall that morning.

concerns: Professor Kim’s gender remains unresolved across frozen sources. The rewrite avoids pronouns and keeps Kim distinct from the Chapter 27 tool-case professor, so no draft contradiction is proved; a human canon ruling is still needed before later copy continuity locks the character.

The packet says “End beat: dead-channel message—‘DUDE. DO NOT FREAK OUT.’” The chapter appropriately continues the exchange to the locked durable state of Kade seeking Mara, but a strict reading could mean the quoted message itself must be the terminal beat; the frozen source and state ledger support the current broader exchange.
strengths: The door reversal gives Kade’s speech a visible, voluntary choice and cleanly pays his established abandonment pattern without letting another character decide for him.
Kade’s speech is specific to Eli and Kade—the food label, model columns, and present-tense “Eli’s worth it” carry the relationship without generic eulogy language.
The rewrite preserves epistemic discipline: Kade refuses false hope from the unmounted name and later distinguishes evidence from proof on NULL-7.
Taren’s blue strip preserves grief without granting absolution, and the unchanged escort distance makes the moral residue concrete.
The closing choice to involve Mara rather than confront Sen or carry the secret alone advances Kade’s human progression and matches the frozen chapter-end state.
Family-clean tone, close-third viewpoint, practical physical business, and audio clarity are strong throughout.
